assimilation_semantics.no_transfer: Run the same worker topology and layer barriers while suppressing all prior-layer outputs.
assimilation_semantics.source_success: Use the standard layered MoA topology and broadcast every immediately prior-layer worker that passes all Core tests with no infrastructure failure.
assimilation_semantics.cumulative_success: Experimental fixed-topology stress policy: broadcast every worker output from every completed layer that passes all Core tests with no infrastructure failure.
assimilation_semantics.no_success_behavior: Broadcast no experience; never substitute partial or failed trajectories.

stress_design.reason_for_task: The clean standard-MoA run retained 3/3 full-Core workers through all four layers while source-success substantially increased input, providing a strong control and a verified-success pool for a cumulative feedback stress test.
stress_design.parallel_sources: Three workers contribute independently verified outputs. If every worker remains Core-verified, cumulative-success workers receive 3, 6, and 9 sources at layers 2, 3, and 4.
stress_design.layer_mechanism: Each new layer independently solves the same task after receiving the policy-selected verified outputs.
stress_design.topology_scope: Worker count, private workspaces, parallel layer execution, layer barriers, and final aggregation remain fixed. Only assimilation history depth changes.
stress_design.canonical_scope: No manager, memory store, worker-specific router, or new agent role is added. Cumulative-success is an experimental assimilation treatment, not canonical one-hop MoA.

validity_gates.control_headroom: Existing no-transfer and source-success arms must retain full layer-4 Core performance.
validity_gates.cumulative_activation: Cumulative-success must receive at least two verified results at layer 2, and its mean received-result count must strictly increase at layers 3 and 4.
validity_gates.integrity: All evaluations must use one checkpoint-2 test collection hash with no infrastructure failure or prohibited benchmark access.

degradation_criteria.primary: Cumulative-success layer-4 mean Core is at least 0.20 below both no-transfer and source-success layer 4.
degradation_criteria.within_arm: Cumulative-success mean Core falls by at least 0.20 from its post-transfer peak to layer 4.
degradation_criteria.curve_shape: At least two post-transfer layer transitions are non-increasing and at least one is strictly decreasing.
degradation_criteria.complexity_support: Cumulative-success received-result count strictly increases from layer 2 through layer 4 and its layer-4 input tokens exceed source-success by at least 20 percent.
degradation_criteria.interpretation: All primary, within-arm, control-headroom, cumulative-activation, complexity-support, and integrity conditions are required before calling the run a degradation curve.

decision_rule.expand: If the curve meets all degradation criteria, repeat twice with counterbalanced arm order.
decision_rule.falsify: If both controls remain strong and cumulative-success remains equally strong, conclude that verified-history accumulation at this depth is insufficient.
decision_rule.invalid: If the controls fail, cumulative transfer does not grow, or evaluation integrity fails, do not interpret performance direction.
